summary: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on Camera String Quartets and both Lieder conditions, with a four-condition OpenScore macro normalised edit distance of 0.2232 against 0.2998. Separate evaluations of lyrics, notation trees and rendered layout reveal complementary aspects of reconstruction and quantify the contribution of layout instructions. Training-stage, reward and candidate-selection studies further examine how recognition changes across model adaptation and decoding.
title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition

summary: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

summary: This record provides the Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) component of the Hi gh-resolution ( d aily and 1 km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over China (HiMIC-Daily) . VPD is a key indicator of moisture stress on vegetation and fire risk, and complements the other five moisture indicators in the collection. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily VPD: Daily 1 km Vapor Pressure Deficit over China, 2003–2025

The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily VPD: Daily 1 km Vapor Pressure Deficit over China, 2003–2025
